# Harbor Fixture

The harbor lights came on one by one along the eastern pier.
“Don’t wait for me,” Mara told the ferryman.
The storm had passed. The boats rocked gently in the dark water.
Jonah tied the last rope and checked the knot twice.
The ferry bell rang out over the quiet grey harbor.
Nobody else remained on the long wooden dock that night.
The clerk locked the office and walked home slowly.
Mara watched the water until the lamps dimmed.
A dog barked twice near the fish market gate.
